question_data.passage:
You are a member of your school's international exchange club. You received the following message from Emma, an exchange student who will arrive next month.

Hi!

Thanks for offering to help me during my stay. I arrive in Osaka on 5 September, and my host family will meet me at the airport, so you don't need to come — but I'd love to see you at school on Monday the 8th.

Two things I want to ask about. First, my host mother says the school has a "cleaning time" every day. Is that right? In my country only the cleaning staff do that, so I'd like to know what I'm supposed to bring. Second, I've been learning Japanese for two years, but almost all of it has been reading. I can write hiragana slowly and I know maybe 200 kanji, so please speak slowly at first — I promise I'll catch up.

I've also signed up for the calligraphy club, because my grandmother collects Japanese brushes and I want to send her something I made myself. Someone told me the club meets on Thursdays after school, but the school website says Wednesdays. Could you check which one is correct before I arrive?

See you soon!
Emma
question_data.subject: 英語
question_data.format_type: 第1問A メッセージ読解

questions.stem: What does Emma ask you to do before she arrives?
choices: Meet her at the airport on 5 September.
Teach her 200 more kanji.
Introduce her to her host family.
Find out which day the calligraphy club meets.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Find out which day the calligraphy club meets.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `Could you check ~?` =「〜を確認してもらえますか」(依頼のコア。`can` より一段丁寧)
- `which one is correct` = 間接疑問。疑問詞のあとが **SV の平叙語順**になる
- `before I arrive` = 時を表す副詞節。未来の内容でも **現在形**で書く

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[Someone told me [(that) the club meets on Thursdays]], but [the school website says [(that) Wednesdays]].`
  前半: S=Someone / V=told / O1=me / O2=that 節 (接続詞 that 省略)
  後半: S=the school website / V=says / O=that 節
`Could you check [which one is correct] [before I arrive]?`
  S=you / V=check / O=間接疑問節 which one is correct / M=before 節

## 📍 本文の根拠
第3段「Someone told me the club meets on Thursdays after school, but the school website says Wednesdays. **Could you check which one is correct before I arrive?**」
依頼は `Could you ~?` の一文だけであり、それ以外の文はすべて状況説明である。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Meet her at the airport on 5 September.」… 第1段 `my host family will meet me at the airport, so you don't need to come` で明確に否定されている。`don't need to` =「する必要がない」。
- 「Teach her 200 more kanji.」… 第2段 `I know maybe 200 kanji` は現状報告であって依頼ではない。依頼文の形 (`Could you ~?`) をとっていない箇所は依頼として数えない。
- 「Introduce her to her host family.」… ホストファミリーは既に決まっていて空港で出迎える側なので、紹介を頼む状況自体が成立しない。

questions.stem: What is true about Emma's Japanese?
choices: She has more experience reading it than writing it.
She has never studied it before.
She can write kanji quickly but cannot read them.
She learned it from her grandmother.
questions.explanation:
正解は「She has more experience reading it than writing it.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `have been ~ing` = 現在完了進行形。「過去のある時点から今まで続いている」がコア
- `almost all of it has been reading` = 主語は「学習の中身」、C が reading (= 読むことだった)
- `can write ~ slowly` = 能力の `can` + 副詞。「できるが速くはない」を含意

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[I've been learning Japanese for two years], but [almost all of it has been reading].`
  前半: S=I / V=have been learning (現在完了進行) / O=Japanese / M=for two years
  後半: S=almost all of it (it = 日本語学習) / V=has been / C=reading
`I can write hiragana slowly and I know maybe 200 kanji.`
  S=I / V=can write / O=hiragana / M=slowly ・ S=I / V=know / O=maybe 200 kanji

## 📍 本文の根拠
第2段「I've been learning Japanese for two years, but **almost all of it has been reading**. I can write hiragana slowly」
`but` を挟んで「2 年学んだ」→「その大半は読むことだった」と限定しており、書く方は `slowly` と但し書きがつく。読む経験 > 書く経験 が読み取れる。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「She has never studied it before.」… `for two years` と正面から矛盾する。現在完了進行形は「今も続いている」ことを示す。
- 「She can write kanji quickly but cannot read them.」… 本文は読む中心・書くのは `slowly` なので、能力の向きが逆になっている。
- 「She learned it from her grandmother.」… 祖母は第3段で `collects Japanese brushes` (筆を集めている) と紹介されるだけで、日本語を教えた人物としては登場しない。

questions.stem: Why did Emma join the calligraphy club?
choices: Her host mother recommended it to her.
She wants to make a present for a member of her family.
It is the only club that meets after school.
She has already practised calligraphy for two years.
questions.explanation:
正解は「She wants to make a present for a member of her family.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `because` = 理由を導く従属接続詞。直後に動機そのものが来る
- `something I made myself` = 目的格の関係代名詞 which/that の省略 + 再帰代名詞 `myself` (「自分の手で」の強調)
- `send 人 物` = 第4文型 (SVOO)。「人に物を送る」

## 🔬 文構造分析
`I've also signed up for the calligraphy club, [because [my grandmother collects Japanese brushes] and [I want to send her [something [(which) I made myself]]]].`
  主節: S=I / V=have signed up / M=for the calligraphy club
  because 節: 等位接続された 2 文
    後半 S=I / V=want to send / O1=her / O2=something + 関係詞節 (which 省略)

## 📍 本文の根拠
第3段「I've also signed up for the calligraphy club, **because my grandmother collects Japanese brushes and I want to send her something I made myself**」
`because` 以下がそのまま入部理由になっている。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Her host mother recommended it to her.」… ホストマザーは第2段で `cleaning time` の話題にのみ登場し、部活を勧めた記述はない。
- 「It is the only club that meets after school.」… 他の部活動についての記述が本文になく、`the only` (唯一) を支える根拠が存在しない。
- 「She has already practised calligraphy for two years.」… 2 年間続けてきたのは第2段の通り日本語の学習であり、書道ではない。期間の係り先の取り違え。

question_data.passage:
You are a first-year student at Minami High School. The school library has posted the following notice on its website.

===========================================
   SUMMER READING CHALLENGE 2026
   Minami High School Library
===========================================

Read, record, and win! The library is running its annual reading challenge from 21 July to 25 August.

HOW IT WORKS
 1. Pick up a Reading Card at the library counter, or download one from the library page.
 2. Each time you finish a book, write the title and one comment of 30 words or more on the card.
 3. Bring the completed card to the counter by 28 August.

LEVELS
 Bronze ( 3 books)  a bookmark designed by the art club
 Silver ( 6 books)  a bookmark and a free drink ticket for the school cafe
 Gold  (10 books)  both of the above, and your review printed in the September library newsletter

RULES
 * Manga and picture books do not count, but graphic novels of more than 100 pages do.
 * Books borrowed from the city library may be included; they do not have to be ours.
 * Comments may be written in English or Japanese, but each comment written in English earns
   you one extra book credit, up to a maximum of three extra credits.

BORROWING DURING THE SUMMER
 The library is open Monday to Friday, 9:00-16:00. It is closed at weekends and from 11 to 15 August.
 You may borrow five books at a time during the summer, instead of the usual two.

WHERE TO READ
 The reading room on the second floor is open during library hours and has thirty seats.
 It is a silent area: talking and eating are not allowed. The counter area on the first
 floor has one small table where you may discuss a book quietly with one other person.

IF YOU FINISH EARLY
 Students who reach Gold before 25 August may keep reading and record extra titles on a
 second card. Extra titles bring no further prize, but the librarian will print the names
 of the three students who read the most in the same September newsletter.

Questions? Email the library staff.
question_data.subject: 英語
question_data.format_type: 第1問B 告知の読み取り

questions.stem: What must you do to receive a prize?
choices: Email a list of the books you have read to the library staff.
Borrow every book you read from the school library.
Write all of your comments in English.
Hand in a card with a written comment for each finished book by 28 August.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Hand in a card with a written comment for each finished book by 28 August.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `Each time SV` =「〜するたびに」(接続詞のはたらきをする名詞句)
- `by 28 August` = 期限の `by`「〜までに (完了)」。継続の `until` とは別物
- 命令文の列挙 (`Pick up ~` / `write ~` / `Bring ~`) = 手順の指示

## 🔬 文構造分析
`Each time [you finish a book], write [the title] and [one comment of 30 words or more] on the card.`
  従属節: S=you / V=finish / O=a book
  主節 (命令文): V=write / O=the title と one comment (等位接続) / M=on the card
`Bring [the completed card] to the counter [by 28 August].`
  V=Bring / O=the completed card / M=to the counter, by 28 August

## 📍 本文の根拠
HOW IT WORKS の 2「**Each time you finish a book, write the title and one comment of 30 words or more on the card.**」と 3「**Bring the completed card to the counter by 28 August.**」
この 2 つが賞を受け取るための手続きのすべてである。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Email a list of the books you have read to the library staff.」… 提出方法はカウンターへの持参と指定されている。メールは末尾で質問窓口として案内されるだけ。
- 「Borrow every book you read from the school library.」… RULES に `Books borrowed from the city library may be included` とあり、学校図書館の本に限る条件は存在しない。
- 「Write all of your comments in English.」… RULES の `Comments may be written in English or Japanese` より英語は任意。英語は追加クレジットが得られる条件であって必須条件ではない。

questions.stem: A student finishes six books and writes all six comments in English. What will that student receive?
choices: A bookmark only.
A bookmark and a free drink ticket.
A bookmark, a drink ticket, and a printed review.
Three bookmarks and a drink ticket.
questions.explanation:
正解は「A bookmark and a free drink ticket.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `up to a maximum of three` =「最大 3 まで」。上限を示す `up to` がこの問題の急所
- `each comment written in English` = 過去分詞の後置修飾「英語で書かれた各コメント」
- `earns you one extra credit` = 第4文型。「あなたに 1 単位をもたらす」

## 🔬 文構造分析
`Comments may be written in English or Japanese, but [each comment [written in English]] earns you [one extra book credit], [up to a maximum of three extra credits].`
  S=each comment (+ 過去分詞句 written in English が後置修飾)
  V=earns / O1=you / O2=one extra book credit / M=up to a maximum of three extra credits

## 📍 本文の根拠
RULES 第3項「each comment written in English earns you one extra book credit, **up to a maximum of three extra credits**」と LEVELS の 「Silver ( 6 books) a bookmark and a free drink ticket」「Gold (10 books)」
6 冊 + 追加 3 = 9 クレジット。Gold の 10 に届かず Silver 止まりになる。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「A bookmark only.」… Bronze (3 冊) は超えているので bookmark だけでは足りない。到達段階の読み違い。
- 「A bookmark, a drink ticket, and a printed review.」… printed review は Gold (10 冊) の特典。上限 3 を無視して 6+6=12 と数えるとこの選択肢に誘導される。`up to a maximum of three` が上限を切っている。
- 「Three bookmarks and a drink ticket.」… bookmark が段階ごとに複数もらえるという記述は LEVELS のどこにもない。

questions.stem: Which of the following books can be counted for the challenge?
choices: A 150-page graphic novel borrowed from the city library.
A manga series borrowed from a friend.
A picture book read to a younger brother.
A 200-page novel that you have not finished.
questions.explanation:
正解は「A 150-page graphic novel borrowed from the city library.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `A do not count, but B do` = 対比の `but` + 代動詞 `do` (= count)。B は算入される
- `of more than 100 pages` = 前置詞句による後置修飾「100 ページを超える〜」
- `may be included` = 許可の `may` の受動態「含めてよい」

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[Manga and picture books] do not count, but [graphic novels [of more than 100 pages]] do.`
  前半: S=Manga and picture books / V=do not count
  後半: S=graphic novels (+ 前置詞句 of more than 100 pages) / V=do (= count の代動詞)
`Books [borrowed from the city library] may be included.`
  S=Books + 過去分詞句 borrowed from the city library / V=may be included

## 📍 本文の根拠
RULES 第1項「Manga and picture books do not count, **but graphic novels of more than 100 pages do**」および第2項「**Books borrowed from the city library may be included**」
150 ページのグラフィックノベルは 100 ページ超で条件を満たし、市立図書館の本でも問題ない。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「A manga series borrowed from a friend.」… `Manga ~ do not count` で明示的に除外されている。
- 「A picture book read to a younger brother.」… `picture books do not count` で明示的に除外されている。
- 「A 200-page novel that you have not finished.」… HOW IT WORKS 2 の `Each time you finish a book` を満たさない。読み終えていない本は記録の対象にならない。

questions.stem: What is different about the library during the summer?
choices: The library opens on Saturday mornings.
The library is open every day from 21 July to 25 August.
Students may borrow more books at one time than they usually can.
Borrowed books may be kept until the end of September.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Students may borrow more books at one time than they usually can.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `instead of ~` =「〜の代わりに」。直前の内容と入れ替わることを示す
- `the usual two` = `the usual` + 数詞で「いつもの 2 冊」。名詞 books の省略
- `during the summer` = 期間限定を示す前置詞句。通常時との対比が前提

## 🔬 文構造分析
`You may borrow [five books] [at a time] [during the summer], [instead of the usual two].`
  S=You / V=may borrow / O=five books
  M=at a time (一度に), during the summer (夏の間), instead of the usual two (通常の 2 冊の代わりに)

## 📍 本文の根拠
BORROWING DURING THE SUMMER「**You may borrow five books at a time during the summer, instead of the usual two.**」
`instead of the usual two` が「普段は 2 冊」という対比を作り、夏だけ増えることを示す。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「The library opens on Saturday mornings.」… `It is closed at weekends` と直接矛盾する。
- 「The library is open every day from 21 July to 25 August.」… `closed at weekends and from 11 to 15 August` があるので「毎日開いている」は成立しない。
- 「Borrowed books may be kept until the end of September.」… 貸出期間についての記述は本文になく、9 月末という日付はどこにも現れない。

question_data.passage:
Your class is choosing a vocabulary app for English homework. Your teacher has given you the following page from a school magazine.

WHICH VOCABULARY APP IS RIGHT FOR YOU?
Three apps compared by our student reporters

--------------------------------------------------------------
                      WordStep      QuizLeaf      MemoRise
--------------------------------------------------------------
 Monthly cost         Free          500 yen       300 yen
 Words in database    3,000         12,000        8,000
 Works offline        Yes           No            Yes
 Speaking practice    No            Yes           Yes
 Daily reminder       Yes           Yes           No
 Progress report      Weekly        Daily         Monthly
--------------------------------------------------------------

HOW WE TESTED
Three student reporters each used one app for eight weeks and kept a record of the words
they studied. We agreed in advance on what we would report: the cost, what the app can and
cannot do, and one thing we would tell a friend. The table above lists only what we could
check ourselves. Ratings from the app stores are not included, because we could not confirm
who had written them.

REVIEWS

Kenta (2nd year): I used WordStep every day on the train, where my phone often loses its signal, and that never caused a problem. The word list is short, though, so I finished it in two months and had nothing left to study. If price is the only thing you care about, start here.

Aya (3rd year): QuizLeaf's speaking check is strict — it told me my "th" sound was wrong about fifty times — but my score on the pronunciation test went up by twelve points. The daily report is useful, yet I cannot open the app on the school bus, because there is no Wi-Fi there. For me, the result was worth the cost.

Sora (1st year): MemoRise sits between the other two. It works on the train and it checks
pronunciation, which is the combination I wanted, and 300 yen is less than I spend on one
drink a week. The weak point is the report. Once a month is too slow to notice that you
have stopped studying; by the time the report arrives you have already lost two weeks. I
set an alarm on my phone instead, which solved the problem but should not have been
necessary. If you are the kind of person who keeps going without being reminded, this is
the one I would choose.
question_data.subject: 英語
question_data.format_type: 第2問A 比較とレビュー

questions.stem: Which app allows a student with no internet connection to practise speaking?
choices: WordStep
MemoRise
QuizLeaf
None of the three apps
questions.explanation:
正解は「MemoRise」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 表の 2 項目を **同時に**満たすものを探す (AND 条件) のがこの形式のコア
- `with no internet connection` = 付帯状況の `with` + 否定「接続がない状態で」
- `allow 人 to do` =「人が〜するのを可能にする」

## 🔬 文構造分析
`Which app allows [a student [with no internet connection]] [to practise speaking]?`
  S=Which app / V=allows / O=a student (+ 前置詞句 with no internet connection が後置修飾) / C=to practise speaking (不定詞)
  → 求める条件は Works offline = Yes **かつ** Speaking practice = Yes

## 📍 本文の根拠
比較表の Works offline 行と Speaking practice 行。
WordStep = Yes / No、QuizLeaf = No / Yes、MemoRise = **Yes / Yes**。
2 条件を同時に満たすのは MemoRise だけである。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「WordStep」… WordStep は Works offline = Yes だが Speaking practice = No。発音練習の機能がない。
- 「QuizLeaf」… QuizLeaf は Speaking practice = Yes だが Works offline = No。Aya も `I cannot open the app on the school bus, because there is no Wi-Fi there` と裏づけている。
- 「None of the three apps」… MemoRise が両方 Yes なので「該当なし」は成立しない。

questions.stem: What problem did Kenta have with WordStep?
choices: The app stopped working when he lost his signal.
He had to pay more than he had expected.
The daily reminder came too often.
He ran out of new words to study.
questions.explanation:
正解は「He ran out of new words to study.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `though` = 譲歩の副詞。文中・文末に置かれ「〜だけれども」と直前の評価を打ち消す
- `had nothing left to study` = `nothing` + 過去分詞 `left` (残された) + 不定詞「勉強するものが残っていなかった」
- `never caused a problem` = 否定の `never`。問題は起きなかった

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[The word list is short], though, so [I finished it in two months] and [had nothing left to study].`
  第1文: S=The word list / V=is / C=short / 挿入=though
  so 以下: S=I / V=finished / O=it / M=in two months
    等位: V=had / O=nothing (+ 過去分詞 left + 不定詞 to study が後置修飾)

## 📍 本文の根拠
Kenta のレビュー「**The word list is short, though, so I finished it in two months and had nothing left to study.**」
収録語数 3,000 という表の数値とも一致する (3 アプリ中で最少)。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「The app stopped working when he lost his signal.」… `that never caused a problem` と正面から矛盾する。電波が切れても支障はなかったと明言している。
- 「He had to pay more than he had expected.」… 表の Monthly cost が Free なので、そもそも支払いが発生しない。
- 「The daily reminder came too often.」… Daily reminder は Yes だが、それを問題として挙げた記述はない。厳しいと述べられているのは QuizLeaf の発音チェックの方。

questions.stem: Which statement about QuizLeaf is an opinion rather than a fact?
choices: The results the app produces are worth what it costs.
The app cannot be used without an internet connection.
The app checks how the user pronounces words.
The app sends the user a report every day.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The results the app produces are worth what it costs.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 事実 = 検証できる記述 / 意見 = 書き手の価値判断。これが区別の唯一の基準
- `For me, ~ was worth the cost` = `For me` (私にとっては) + 価値語 `worth`。**典型的な意見マーカー**
- 表に載っている項目は原則として事実側

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[For me], [the result] was [worth the cost].`
  M=For me (話し手限定の視点) / S=the result / V=was / C=worth the cost (形容詞句)
  → 主語が話し手の評価対象であり、`worth` という価値判断語が C に立つ = 意見

## 📍 本文の根拠
Aya のレビュー最終文「**For me, the result was worth the cost.**」
`For me` が「人によって違いうる」ことを示しており、検証可能な事実ではない。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「The app cannot be used without an internet connection.」… 表 Works offline = No で確認できる**事実**。Aya の `there is no Wi-Fi there` も同じ事実を裏づける。
- 「The app checks how the user pronounces words.」… 表 Speaking practice = Yes で確認できる**事実**。`QuizLeaf's speaking check is strict` も機能の存在を前提にしている。
- 「The app sends the user a report every day.」… 表 Progress report = Daily で確認できる**事実**。

questions.stem: A student wants an app that costs nothing and reminds them to study every day. Which app fits?
choices: QuizLeaf
MemoRise
WordStep
Either QuizLeaf or MemoRise
questions.explanation:
正解は「WordStep」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- ここも AND 条件。`costs nothing` (無料) **かつ** `reminds them every day` (毎日通知)
- `cost nothing` = 動詞 `cost` + `nothing`「費用がかからない」
- `remind 人 to do` =「人に〜するよう思い出させる」

## 🔬 文構造分析
`A student wants [an app [that costs nothing]] and [reminds them to study every day].`
  S=A student / V=wants / O=an app + 関係詞節
  関係詞節 that costs nothing / (that) reminds them to study every day … 2 つが and で並列
  → 関係詞 that の先行詞は共通で an app。よって両方を満たす 1 つのアプリを探す

## 📍 本文の根拠
比較表の Monthly cost 行と Daily reminder 行。
WordStep = **Free / Yes**、QuizLeaf = 500 yen / Yes、MemoRise = 300 yen / No。
Kenta の `If price is the only thing you care about, start here.` も後押しになる。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「QuizLeaf」… QuizLeaf は Daily reminder = Yes だが Monthly cost が 500 yen で無料ではない。
- 「MemoRise」… MemoRise は 300 yen かかるうえ Daily reminder = No。2 条件とも満たさない。
- 「Either QuizLeaf or MemoRise」… QuizLeaf も MemoRise も有料なので、どちらでもよいという選択にはならない。

questions.stem: According to the reviews, what happened to Aya after she used QuizLeaf?
choices: She stopped taking the school bus.
Her score on a pronunciation test improved.
She was able to study offline for the first time.
She learned all 12,000 words in the database.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Her score on a pronunciation test improved.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `go up by ~` =「〜だけ上がる」。`by` は差・程度を表す前置詞 (増減幅のコア)
- `my score on the pronunciation test` = `on` が「〜における得点」の対象を示す
- 逆接 `but` の後ろに書き手が本当に言いたい結果が来る

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[QuizLeaf's speaking check is strict] — it told me my "th" sound was wrong about fifty times — but [my score on the pronunciation test went up by twelve points].`
  前半: S=QuizLeaf's speaking check / V=is / C=strict
  ダッシュ挿入: S=it / V=told / O1=me / O2=that 節 (that 省略)
  but 以下: S=my score on the pronunciation test / V=went up / M=by twelve points

## 📍 本文の根拠
Aya のレビュー「but **my score on the pronunciation test went up by twelve points**」
`but` の後ろが結果であり、これが設問の問う「何が起きたか」にあたる。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「She stopped taking the school bus.」… バスでアプリが開けないと述べているだけで、バス通学をやめたとは書かれていない。因果の飛躍。
- 「She was able to study offline for the first time.」… 表の Works offline = No。QuizLeaf ではオフライン学習はできない。
- 「She learned all 12,000 words in the database.」… 12,000 は表にある収録語数であって、Aya が覚えた語数ではない。数値の係り先の取り違え。

question_data.passage:
You are writing a report about school schedules. You have found the following article in a school newspaper written by a student committee.

SHOULD OUR SCHOOL DAY START LATER?
by the Student Life Committee, Kita High School

Last month our committee asked all 612 students at this school about the daily schedule, and 478 students answered. Of those, 61% said that they usually sleep fewer than six hours on school nights, and 74% said that they feel sleepy during first period.

Our school day begins at 8:20, which is fifteen minutes earlier than the average starting time for public high schools in this city. Students who travel by train from the west side of the city have to leave home before 7:00.

We think that a later start would help. A study carried out at a high school in another prefecture found that when the first class was moved from 8:15 to 8:45, the number of students arriving late fell by 40% over one term. The same report noted that average test scores in the first-period subject rose slightly, though the researchers themselves said that the change was too small to be certain about.

Of course, a later start means a later finish. Club activities would lose about thirty minutes of practice time on weekdays, and several teachers have told us that this is the most serious problem with the idea. Our committee believes that shorter but better-organised practice would be no less effective, and that arriving at school awake matters more than half an hour on the field.

We also asked what students would do with an extra thirty minutes in the morning. The most
common answer was sleep (58%), followed by breakfast (21%) and study (11%). Only 4% chose
club activities. Among the 129 students who travel by train, 88 said they had fallen asleep
on the train at least once in the past month.

Two teachers replied to our request for comments. Mr Okada, who coaches the baseball team,
told us that a thirty-minute loss on weekdays would be difficult to make up at weekends,
because the ground is shared with three other schools. Ms Fujita, who teaches first-period
mathematics, said that she now spends the first ten minutes of most lessons waking the class
up, and that she would rather start later and teach for the full period.

We will present these results to the school council in October.
question_data.subject: 英語
question_data.format_type: 第2問B 記事(事実と意見)

questions.stem: What did the committee's survey find?
choices: All 612 students at the school answered the survey.
Most students want the school day to begin at 8:45.
Students from the west side of the city arrive late most often.
About three-quarters of the students who replied feel sleepy in the first class.
questions.explanation:
正解は「About three-quarters of the students who replied feel sleepy in the first class.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `Of those, 74% said ~` = `those` が直前の「回答した 478 人」を受ける。**母数は回答者**
- `three-quarters` = 4 分の 3 (= 75%)。74% の言い換え
- `feel sleepy` = 感覚動詞 feel + 形容詞

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[Of those], [61% said [(that) they usually sleep fewer than six hours on school nights]], and [74% said [(that) they feel sleepy during first period]].`
  M=Of those (回答した 478 人のうち)
  S=74% / V=said / O=that 節 (S=they / V=feel / C=sleepy / M=during first period)

## 📍 本文の根拠
第1段「our committee asked all 612 students at this school ~, and 478 students answered. Of those, 61% ~, and **74% said that they feel sleepy during first period**」
74% ≒ 4 分の 3 で、母数は「回答した生徒」である。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「All 612 students at the school answered the survey.」… `our committee asked all 612 students ~ and 478 students answered` より、回答したのは 478 人。全員ではない。`asked` と `answered` の主語の違いが急所。
- 「Most students want the school day to begin at 8:45.」… 8:45 は第3段で紹介される**他県の高校の事例**の時刻であり、この学校の生徒の希望として調査された事実はない。
- 「Students from the west side of the city arrive late most often.」… 西側から通う生徒については `have to leave home before 7:00` とあるだけで、遅刻が最も多いという記述はない。

questions.stem: Which of the following is a fact stated in the article?
choices: A later start would help the students at this school.
Shorter practice can be just as effective as longer practice.
The school day at Kita High School starts fifteen minutes earlier than the city average.
Coming to school awake matters more than extra practice time.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The school day at Kita High School starts fifteen minutes earlier than the city average.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 事実 = 数値・出来事など検証できるもの / 意見 = `We think` `believes` を伴う主張
- `fifteen minutes earlier than ~` = 比較級 + 差の表現。数値で確認できる = 事実
- 意見マーカー: `We think` / `Our committee believes` / `matters more than`

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[Our school day] begins [at 8:20], [which is fifteen minutes earlier than [the average starting time for public high schools in this city]].`
  S=Our school day / V=begins / M=at 8:20
  which 節 = 非制限用法の関係代名詞 (先行詞は at 8:20 という内容)
    S=which / V=is / C=fifteen minutes earlier than ~ (比較級 + 差 fifteen minutes)

## 📍 本文の根拠
第2段「**Our school day begins at 8:20, which is fifteen minutes earlier than the average starting time for public high schools in this city.**」
時刻の比較という検証可能な記述であり、意見マーカーを伴わない。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「A later start would help the students at this school.」… 第3段冒頭 `**We think** that a later start would help.` の内容そのもので、意見。
- 「Shorter practice can be just as effective as longer practice.」… 最終段 `Our committee **believes** that shorter but better-organised practice would be no less effective` の内容で、意見。
- 「Coming to school awake matters more than extra practice time.」… 同じく最終段の `Our committee believes ~ that arriving at school awake **matters more than** half an hour on the field` の内容で、価値判断。

questions.stem: Which of the following is an opinion stated in the article?
choices: 478 of the 612 students answered the survey.
Practice that is shorter but better organised would be just as effective.
At a school in another prefecture, late arrivals fell by 40% in one term.
Students from the west side of the city have to leave home before 7:00.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Practice that is shorter but better organised would be just as effective.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `no less effective` = `no + 比較級`「決して劣らない = 同じくらい効果的」。強い主張のコア
- `believes that ~` = 意見であることを明示する動詞
- `shorter but better-organised` = 譲歩を含む形容詞の並列

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[Our committee] believes [that [shorter but better-organised practice] would be [no less effective]].`
  S=Our committee / V=believes / O=that 節
  that 節: S=shorter but better-organised practice / V=would be / C=no less effective
  → 主節の V が believes である時点で、that 節の中身は検証済みの事実ではなく主張

## 📍 本文の根拠
最終段「**Our committee believes that shorter but better-organised practice would be no less effective**」
根拠となるデータは示されておらず、委員会の判断として述べられている。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「478 of the 612 students answered the survey.」… 第1段の調査結果の数値そのもので、検証可能な**事実**。
- 「At a school in another prefecture, late arrivals fell by 40% in one term.」… 第3段で紹介される他県の研究結果の数値で、**事実**として提示されている。
- 「Students from the west side of the city have to leave home before 7:00.」… 第2段 `Students who travel by train from the west side of the city have to leave home before 7:00` は通学の実態を述べた**事実**。時刻という検証できる情報しか含まない。

questions.stem: What does the article say about the study from another prefecture?
choices: Its finding about test scores was not strong enough to be sure of.
It showed that test scores fell after the change.
It was carried out over a period of three years.
It found no change in the number of students arriving late.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Its finding about test scores was not strong enough to be sure of.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `though` = 譲歩の接続詞。直前の肯定的な内容に留保をつける
- `too small to be certain about` = `too ~ to do`「〜すぎて…できない」。**断定できない**が結論
- `rose slightly` = 上がったが `slightly` (わずかに) と限定

## 🔬 文構造分析
`The same report noted [that [average test scores in the first-period subject] rose slightly], [though [the researchers themselves said [that [the change] was [too small to be certain about]]]].`
  主節: S=The same report / V=noted / O=that 節 (S=average test scores / V=rose / M=slightly)
  though 節: S=the researchers themselves / V=said / O=that 節
    that 節: S=the change / V=was / C=too small to be certain about

## 📍 本文の根拠
第3段「average test scores in the first-period subject rose slightly, **though the researchers themselves said that the change was too small to be certain about**」
`too ~ to ...` が「確信できるほどではない」という否定的結論を作っている。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「It showed that test scores fell after the change.」… `rose` (上がった) と書かれており、下がったのではない。動詞の意味の取り違え。
- 「It was carried out over a period of three years.」… 調査期間は `over one term` (1 学期間) と明記されている。3 年間ではない。
- 「It found no change in the number of students arriving late.」… `the number of students arriving late fell by 40%` と明記されている。変化がなかったという記述と正反対。

questions.stem: What will the committee do next?
choices: Ask the teachers to shorten club activities.
Change the starting time to 8:45 in October.
Carry out a second survey of all 612 students.
Report the results of the survey to the school council.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Report the results of the survey to the school council.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `will present` = 未来の予定。設問「次に何をするか」に直結する
- `present A to B` =「A を B に提示する」
- `in October` = 予定の時期。この時期に何をするのかを取り違えない

## 🔬 文構造分析
`We will present [these results] [to the school council] [in October].`
  S=We (= the Student Life Committee) / V=will present / O=these results
  M=to the school council (提示先), in October (時期)

## 📍 本文の根拠
最終行「**We will present these results to the school council in October.**」
記事全体の締めくくりであり、次の行動を述べた唯一の文である。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Ask the teachers to shorten club activities.」… 部活動の時間短縮は始業を遅らせた場合に生じる帰結として触れられているだけで、教員に依頼するとは述べていない。
- 「Change the starting time to 8:45 in October.」… 10 月に行うのは**報告**であって、始業時刻の変更ではない。変更は評議会に諮る段階にすら至っていない。
- 「Carry out a second survey of all 612 students.」… 2 回目の調査についての記述は本文にない。

question_data.passage:
You are reading the online newsletter of your school's volunteer club.

RICE FIELDS AND WET SOCKS
by Nao, second year

I had never stood in a rice field before last Saturday. Twenty-two of us took the 6:40 train to Kawakami, a village about an hour north of the city, to help with the planting. Mr Ito, the farmer who invited us, has grown rice on the same land for forty years and now works it alone.

He gave us five minutes of instruction. Push the seedling in until the roots are covered, he said, no deeper, and keep to the line marked by the rope. Then he stepped back and let us try. My first row was a disaster. Half of my seedlings floated back up within a minute, and I had pushed the others so far down that Mr Ito had to pull them out again.

What surprised me was the mud. I had expected it to be soft. In fact it grips your feet and does not let go, and lifting one leg while balancing on the other is far harder than it looks. Three people fell in. By eleven o'clock nobody cared any more about staying clean.

We finished four fields before lunch, which Mr Ito said would have taken him three days on his own. He would not accept anything for the meal his wife had prepared.

The club returns in September for the harvest. Sign up at the club room by 5 August. We can take twenty-five people this time, and no experience is needed.
question_data.subject: 英語

questions.stem: What surprised Nao most about the work?
choices: How long the train journey took.
How many people Mr Ito employed.
How cold the water in the field was.
How hard it was to move through the mud.
questions.explanation:
正解は「How hard it was to move through the mud.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `What surprised me was ~` = 強調構文的な what 節。**驚いた対象**が be 動詞の後ろに来る
- `I had expected it to be soft. In fact ~` = 予想と現実の対比。`In fact` の後ろが実際
- `grip` =「つかんで離さない」。柔らかさの逆を表す動詞がコア

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[What surprised me] was [the mud].`
  S=What surprised me (関係代名詞 what 節) / V=was / C=the mud
`In fact [it] grips [your feet] and does not let go, and [lifting one leg while balancing on the other] is [far harder than it looks].`
  前半: S=it (= the mud) / V=grips / O=your feet ・ V=does not let go
  後半: S=動名詞句 lifting one leg ~ / V=is / C=far harder than it looks

## 📍 本文の根拠
第4段「**What surprised me was the mud.** I had expected it to be soft. In fact it grips your feet and does not let go, and lifting one leg while balancing on the other is far harder than it looks.」
`What surprised me was ~` が「最も驚いたこと」を名指ししている。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「How long the train journey took.」… 電車は `the 6:40 train` `about an hour north of the city` と述べられるだけで、所要時間に驚いたという記述はない。
- 「How many people Mr Ito employed.」… 第1段に `now works it alone` (今は一人で耕している) とあり、雇っている人はいない。むしろ人手がないことが招待の背景になっている。
- 「How cold the water in the field was.」… 水の冷たさについての記述は本文にない。驚いたのは泥の「柔らかさの予想が外れたこと」。

questions.stem: What will the club do in September?
choices: Invite Mr Ito to visit the school.
Plant rice in a different village.
Return to Kawakami to help with the harvest.
Send Nao to work in the field alone.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Return to Kawakami to help with the harvest.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `return` =「戻る」。同じ場所への再訪を含意する
- `for the harvest` = 目的の for。「収穫のために」
- `Sign up ~ by 5 August` = 期限の by。締切であって実施日ではない

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[The club] returns [in September] [for the harvest].`
  S=The club / V=returns (確定した予定を表す現在形) / M=in September, for the harvest
`Sign up [at the club room] [by 5 August].`
  命令文: V=Sign up / M=at the club room, by 5 August

## 📍 本文の根拠
最終段「**The club returns in September for the harvest.** Sign up at the club room by 5 August.」
9 月の予定は「収穫の手伝いに戻る」こと。8 月 5 日は申込の締切であって活動日ではない。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Invite Mr Ito to visit the school.」… Mr Ito が学校を訪れるという記述はない。訪れるのは部員の側。
- 「Plant rice in a different village.」… `returns` は同じ場所に戻ることを示す。別の村へ行くとは述べられていない。
- 「Send Nao to work in the field alone.」… `We can take twenty-five people this time` と 25 人規模の活動であり、Nao が単独で作業するという記述はない。

You are reading a blog written by a Japanese high school student who took part in an international science camp.

MY WEEK AT THE PACIFIC SCIENCE CAMP
Posted by Sora | 12 August

When my teacher handed me the application form in April, I almost gave it straight back. The camp was to be held entirely in English, and I had never spoken English outside a classroom. My teacher only said, "Write the essay first, then decide." So I wrote it, and three weeks later an email told me that I had been chosen as one of forty students from eleven countries.

I spent May and June in a quiet panic. I made a list of two hundred science words and tested myself on it every morning on the bus. Looking back, that list was the least useful thing I did, because nobody at the camp talked like a textbook.

Day 1. We were put into teams of five and told that by Friday each team had to present a solution to a local problem. My team had a student from Chile, one from Kenya, one from Thailand and one from Australia. For the first hour I said almost nothing. Ana, from Chile, noticed and asked me a question directly. I answered in five words. She waited, and then said, "Okay, so you mean ..." and repeated my idea as a full sentence. Nobody laughed.

Day 2. Our problem was the plastic waste washing up on the beach two kilometres from the camp. We spent the morning collecting and sorting rubbish. Kwame, from Kenya, kept asking "why" about everything: why did most of the bottles have foreign labels, why were the pieces smaller near the river mouth. By lunchtime we had thrown out our first idea completely.

Day 3. This was the day I stopped translating. I was explaining how a filter my grandfather uses for rice-field water might be adapted, and halfway through I realised that I had not thought in Japanese for several minutes. My grammar was poor. It did not seem to matter.

Day 4. We built a model, and it failed twice. Ana wanted to redesign it; Kwame wanted to test the same model again first. They argued for twenty minutes. In the end we did both, and I was the one who suggested it — my first complete idea in English.

Day 5. We presented. We did not win; a team from Thailand did, with a much simpler idea. But the judge who spoke to us afterwards said that our team had changed its mind more often than any other team, and that he meant this as a compliment.

I came home with the two-hundred-word list still in my bag, mostly unused. What I actually brought back is smaller and harder to explain: I now know what it feels like to be understood by someone who is not simply being polite.
question_data.subject: 英語
question_data.format_type: 第3問B 体験ブログ(時系列)

questions.stem: What did Sora do first, immediately after receiving the application form?
choices: Made a list of two hundred science words.
Returned the form to the teacher without applying.
Wrote the essay that the application required.
Sent an email to the camp organisers.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Wrote the essay that the application required.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `almost gave it straight back` = `almost` +過去形「危うく〜するところだった (実際にはしなかった)」
- `Write the essay first, then decide.` = 命令文。先生の助言が行動の順序を決めている
- `So I wrote it` の `So` が助言→実行の因果をつなぐ

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[When my teacher handed me the application form in April], I almost gave it straight back.`
  従属節: S=my teacher / V=handed / O1=me / O2=the application form / M=in April
  主節: S=I / V=almost gave back / O=it → `almost` により**実際には返していない**
`My teacher only said, "Write the essay first, then decide." So I wrote it.`
  S=I / V=wrote / O=it (= the essay)

## 📍 本文の根拠
第1段「When my teacher handed me the application form in April, I almost gave it straight back. ~ My teacher only said, "Write the essay first, then decide." **So I wrote it**」
用紙を受け取った直後の行動はエッセイを書くことである。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Made a list of two hundred science words.」… 単語リストを作ったのは第2段の `I spent May and June` の時期で、合格の知らせを受けた**後**。時系列が逆。
- 「Returned the form to the teacher without applying.」… `almost gave it straight back` は「危うく返しかけた」であって、実際には返していない。`almost` の処理が急所。
- 「Sent an email to the camp organisers.」… メールは `an email told me that I had been chosen` と、受け取った側として登場する。送ってはいない。

questions.stem: Which of these happened last?
choices: Sora's team gave up their first idea.
Sora made a suggestion that the whole team accepted.
Sora realised that he had stopped translating in his head.
Sora learned that he had been chosen for the camp.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Sora made a suggestion that the whole team accepted.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- ブログは日付順 (Day 1〜Day 5) に並ぶので、**どの日の出来事か**を特定すれば順序が決まる
- `In the end we did both` = 議論の決着を示す。その直後が Sora の行動
- `I was the one who suggested it` = 強調構文的な `the one who`「〜したのは私だった」

## 🔬 文構造分析
`In the end [we did both], and [I was [the one [who suggested it]]] — my first complete idea in English.`
  前半: S=we / V=did / O=both
  後半: S=I / V=was / C=the one + 関係詞節 who suggested it
  同格のダッシュ: my first complete idea in English が it を言い換える

## 📍 本文の根拠
Day 4「In the end we did both, and **I was the one who suggested it** — my first complete idea in English.」
選択肢の出来事は Day 4 / Day 2 / Day 3 / 4〜5月 に対応し、最も遅いのが Day 4。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Sora's team gave up their first idea.」… Day 2 の `By lunchtime we had thrown out our first idea completely` で、Day 4 より前。
- 「Sora realised that he had stopped translating in his head.」… Day 3 の `This was the day I stopped translating` で、Day 4 より前。
- 「Sora learned that he had been chosen for the camp.」… 第1段の `three weeks later an email told me that I had been chosen` で、キャンプ開始前 (4〜5月)。最も早い出来事。

questions.stem: Why does Sora call the word list "the least useful thing" he did?
choices: He lost the list on the first day of the camp.
The camp turned out to be held in Japanese.
The other students had already learned all the words on it.
The English actually used at the camp was not like the English in a textbook.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The English actually used at the camp was not like the English in a textbook.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `nobody talked like a textbook` = 否定の主語 `nobody` +様態の `like`「教科書のようには話さなかった」
- `the least useful thing` = 最上級の否定的用法「最も役に立たなかったもの」
- `because` が理由を直接示す

## 🔬 文構造分析
`Looking back, [that list] was [the least useful thing [I did]], [because [nobody at the camp talked like a textbook]].`
  分詞構文: Looking back (振り返ると)
  主節: S=that list / V=was / C=the least useful thing + 関係詞節 (that 省略) I did
  because 節: S=nobody at the camp / V=talked / M=like a textbook

## 📍 本文の根拠
第2段「Looking back, that list was the least useful thing I did, **because nobody at the camp talked like a textbook**」
理由は `because` 以下に明示されている。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「He lost the list on the first day of the camp.」… 最終段に `the two-hundred-word list still in my bag` とあり、紛失していない。
- 「The camp turned out to be held in Japanese.」… 第1段に `The camp was to be held entirely in English` とあり、英語で行われた。
- 「The other students had already learned all the words on it.」… 他の参加者がその単語を知っていたかどうかは本文で一切触れられていない。

questions.stem: What did the judge praise Sora's team for?
choices: Being willing to change their ideas.
Presenting the simplest solution of all the teams.
Building a model that worked at the first attempt.
Speaking the most fluent English.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Being willing to change their ideas.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `changed its mind` =「考えを変えた」。`mind` は単数で「意向」
- `more often than any other team` = 比較級 + `any other` で事実上の最上級
- `he meant this as a compliment` = 一見否定的な内容を**褒め言葉**として述べたと明示

## 🔬 文構造分析
`the judge [who spoke to us afterwards] said [that [our team had changed its mind more often than any other team]], and [that he meant this as a compliment].`
  S=the judge + 関係詞節 who spoke to us afterwards / V=said / O=that 節 × 2 (and で並列)
  第1の that 節: S=our team / V=had changed (過去完了) / O=its mind / M=more often than any other team

## 📍 本文の根拠
Day 5「the judge who spoke to us afterwards said that **our team had changed its mind more often than any other team, and that he meant this as a compliment**」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Presenting the simplest solution of all the teams.」… `a team from Thailand did, with a much simpler idea` とあり、最も簡単な案で勝ったのは別のチーム。
- 「Building a model that worked at the first attempt.」… Day 4 に `We built a model, and it failed twice` とある。一度で成功していない。
- 「Speaking the most fluent English.」… 英語の流暢さについて審査員が言及した記述はない。Sora 自身も `My grammar was poor` と述べている。

questions.stem: What does Sora suggest that he gained from the camp?
choices: A large vocabulary of scientific terms.
A prize for the best presentation at the camp.
A sense of what it is like to communicate real meaning in English.
A decision to study science at university.
questions.explanation:
正解は「A sense of what it is like to communicate real meaning in English.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `what it feels like to ~` =「〜するのがどんな感じか」。体験知を表す定型
- `be understood` = 受動態「理解される」
- `who is not simply being polite` = 進行形の `being polite`「その場だけ礼儀正しくふるまう」の否定

## 🔬 文構造分析
`I now know [what it feels like [to be understood by [someone [who is not simply being polite]]]].`
  S=I / M=now / V=know / O=what 節
  what 節: it = 形式主語、真主語 = to be understood ~ (不定詞句)
  関係詞節 who is not simply being polite が someone を修飾

## 📍 本文の根拠
最終段「What I actually brought back is smaller and harder to explain: **I now know what it feels like to be understood by someone who is not simply being polite.**」
コロンの後がブログ全体の結論にあたる。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「A large vocabulary of scientific terms.」… 単語リストは `mostly unused` (ほとんど使わなかった) と述べられている。得たものとして正面から否定されている。
- 「A prize for the best presentation at the camp.」… `We did not win; a team from Thailand did` とあり、賞は取っていない。
- 「A decision to study science at university.」… 大学進学や専攻についての記述は本文にない。

question_data.passage:
Your class is preparing a presentation about how students travel to school. You have found two short reports.

REPORT A (from a city education office newsletter)

In June we surveyed 1,200 high school students in Higashi City about how they travel to school. The results are shown below. We also asked students to rate their journey from 1 (very unpleasant) to 5 (very pleasant).

   Method     Students    Average time    Average rating
   Train         468         42 min            2.9
   Bicycle       372         24 min            3.8
   Bus           204         35 min            2.6
   Walking       156         18 min            4.1

Students who cycle or walk gave clearly higher ratings than those who use public transport. The groups differ in one other way, however: almost all of the students who walk live within 1.5 km of their school.

We also asked what students disliked most about their journey. Among cyclists the most common answer was rain, mentioned by 63%; among walkers it was heavy bags. Neither group mentioned other people. For train and bus users, four of the five most common answers involved other passengers.

One further point deserves attention. We asked students to record their actual departure time for one week. The times students had given us from memory were, on average, seven minutes later than the times they recorded. The gap was largest among train users, who underestimated by eleven minutes. This suggests that reported journey times in surveys of this kind should be treated as a lower limit rather than an exact figure.

Finally, a caution about the ratings themselves. Students rated the journey they actually make, not the journey they would make by another method. A student who walks 1.2 km has no view on what the same trip would feel like by train, and a train user cannot walk 18 km. The ratings therefore compare people, not methods, and any conclusion drawn from them carries that limit.

REPORT B (from the student newspaper of Higashi North High School)

We repeated the city survey at our own school, where 84% of students come by train. Our average rating for the train journey was 2.2 — much lower than the city figure of 2.9. When we asked why, the most common answer was not the length of the journey but the crowding: 71% of train users said that they could not sit down, and 55% said that they could not read or study on board.

One result surprised us. Students who had to change trains once rated their journey higher (2.6) than students who took a single direct train (2.1). In interviews, several students explained that the change gave them a short break and a chance to get a seat on the second train. One student put it this way: "Standing for forty minutes is worse than standing for twenty, sitting for five, and standing for fifteen, even though the total is the same."

We asked the same students what would improve their journey most. Only 9% chose a faster train. 46% chose a less crowded train, and 28% chose a guaranteed seat even if the journey took longer. When we put these results beside the city figures, one pattern stands out: the two surveys agree about which groups are least satisfied, but they disagree about why. The city report treats the journey as a length of time. Our respondents treat it as a length of time spent in a particular condition, and it is the condition, not the clock, that they complain about.

question_data.format_type: 第4問 複数資料の統合

questions.stem: According to Report A, which group spends the least time travelling to school?
choices: Students who walk.
Students who cycle.
Students who take the bus.
Students who take the train.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Students who walk.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 表は**どの列を見るか**で答えが変わる。設問の `time` は Average time 列
- `the least time` = 最上級。最小値を選ぶ
- 人数 (Students 列) と所要時間 (Average time 列) を取り違えないのがこの形式の急所

## 🔬 文構造分析
`Which group spends [the least time] [travelling to school]?`
  S=Which group / V=spends / O=the least time / M=travelling to school (分詞句)
  → `spend + 時間 + doing`「〜するのに時間を費やす」の型

## 📍 本文の根拠
REPORT A の表 Average time 列: Train 42 min / Bicycle 24 min / Bus 35 min / **Walking 18 min**。
最小は Walking の 18 分。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Students who cycle.」… Bicycle は 24 min で Walking より長い。
- 「Students who take the bus.」… Bus は 35 min。Walking の約 2 倍。
- 「Students who take the train.」… Train は 42 min で 4 群の中で最長。最小と最大の取り違え。

questions.stem: According to Report A, how many of the students surveyed use public transport?
questions.explanation:
正解は「672」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `public transport` = 公共交通機関。ここでは Train と Bus の 2 つを指す
- 表の複数行を**足す**タイプの設問。どの行が該当するかの判断が本体
- 自転車・徒歩は公共交通機関に含まれない

## 🔬 文構造分析
`How many students [surveyed] use [public transport]?`
  S=How many students + 過去分詞 surveyed が後置修飾 (調査対象の生徒)
  V=use / O=public transport
  → 該当する行 = Train (468) + Bus (204)

## 📍 本文の根拠
REPORT A の表 Students 列: Train **468** / Bicycle 372 / Bus **204** / Walking 156。
468 + 204 = 672。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「468」… 468 は Train のみの人数。Bus を足し忘れている。
- 「528」… 528 は Bicycle 372 + Walking 156 で、公共交通機関**ではない**方の合計。
- 「1,200」… 1,200 は調査対象全体の人数。4 群すべての合計であり、公共交通機関に限らない。

questions.stem: What does Report A suggest about the high ratings given by students who walk?
choices: They show that walking is more comfortable than cycling in every case.
They may be partly explained by the short distances those students live from school.
They are based on a much larger sample than the other groups.
They were collected in a different month from the rest of the data.
questions.explanation:
正解は「They may be partly explained by the short distances those students live from school.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `however` = 転換の副詞。**直前の結論に別の説明を持ち込む**合図
- `differ in ~` =「〜の点で異なる」
- `almost all of ~ live within 1.5 km` = 距離という交絡要因の提示

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[The groups] differ [in one other way], however: [almost all of [the students [who walk]]] live [within 1.5 km of their school].`
  第1文: S=The groups / V=differ / M=in one other way / 挿入=however
  コロン以下: S=almost all of the students + 関係詞節 who walk / V=live / M=within 1.5 km of their school

## 📍 本文の根拠
REPORT A 末尾「Students who cycle or walk gave clearly higher ratings ~. **The groups differ in one other way, however: almost all of the students who walk live within 1.5 km of their school.**」
`however` 以下が、高評価を距離という別要因で説明しうると示唆している。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「They show that walking is more comfortable than cycling in every case.」… 自転車との比較で「あらゆる場合に」と言い切る根拠は本文にない。`in every case` は本文より強すぎる一般化。
- 「They are based on a much larger sample than the other groups.」… Walking は 156 人で 4 群中**最少**。標本が大きいという記述と逆。
- 「They were collected in a different month from the rest of the data.」… 調査は `In June we surveyed` と一括で行われている。別の月ではない。

questions.stem: According to Report B, what do train users at Higashi North High School dislike most?
choices: The journey takes too long.
The trains are often late.
The fares are too expensive.
The trains are too crowded.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The trains are too crowded.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `not A but B` = 「A ではなく B」。**A を明確に否定する**構文
- `the most common answer` = 最も多かった回答 = 主たる理由
- `crowding` = 混雑。動名詞から派生した名詞

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[The most common answer] was [not [the length of the journey] but [the crowding]]: [71% said [(that) they could not sit down]], and [55% said [(that) they could not read or study on board]].`
  S=The most common answer / V=was / C=not A but B
    A=the length of the journey (否定される) / B=the crowding (これが答え)
  コロン以下が B の具体的な内訳

## 📍 本文の根拠
REPORT B「the most common answer was **not the length of the journey but the crowding**: 71% of train users said that they could not sit down」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「The journey takes too long.」… `not the length of the journey` で**明示的に否定**されている。not A but B の A にあたる。
- 「The trains are often late.」… 遅延についての記述は本文に一切ない。
- 「The fares are too expensive.」… 運賃についての記述も本文に一切ない。

questions.stem: Which conclusion is supported by both reports?
choices: A shorter journey is not always rated as a better one.
The students who travel longest are always the least satisfied.
Users of public transport are more satisfied than cyclists.
The city survey and the school survey produced the same results.
questions.explanation:
正解は「A shorter journey is not always rated as a better one.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 「両方の資料が支持する結論」= どちらにも反例がない選択肢を選ぶ
- `not always` = 部分否定「必ずしも〜ではない」。**1 つでも反例があれば成り立つ**
- `always` を含む選択肢は反例 1 つで崩れる (全称命題)

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[A shorter journey] is [not always] rated [as a better one].`
  S=A shorter journey / V=is rated (受動態) / C=as a better one / M=not always (部分否定)
  → 「短い方が高評価」が**常には**成り立たないことを 1 例でも示せばよい

## 📍 本文の根拠
REPORT A: Train 42 min = 2.9 に対し Bus 35 min = 2.6。**より短いバスの方が低評価**で、所要時間と満足度が単純に対応していない。
REPORT B:「the most common answer was **not the length of the journey but the crowding**」と、所要時間が主因であることを正面から否定している。さらに「Students who had to change trains once rated their journey higher (2.6) than students who took a single direct train (2.1).」も同じ向きの例。
2 つの資料のどちらにも反例があるので、部分否定 `not always` が支持される。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「The students who travel longest are always the least satisfied.」… `always` を含む全称命題。REPORT A の Train (42 min・2.9) > Bus (35 min・2.6) が反例になる。
- 「Users of public transport are more satisfied than cyclists.」… REPORT A で Bicycle 3.8 は Train 2.9・Bus 2.6 より高い。逆の記述。
- 「The city survey and the school survey produced the same results.」… REPORT B は自校の train 評価 2.2 が市の 2.9 より `much lower` と明記しており、同一の結果ではない。

question_data.passage:
You are preparing a presentation for your English class about a person introduced in a magazine article. Read the article and organise the information.

THE WOMAN WHO DREW WHAT NOBODY COULD SEE

Ines Bertrand was born in 1901 in a small town in the south of France, the fourth of six children. Her father repaired clocks. There was no money for the art school she wanted to attend, so at sixteen she took a job painting numbers onto clock faces in her father's workshop — work that demanded a steady hand and a very fine brush.

In 1922 a visiting university lecturer, Dr Hugo Meyer, brought a broken microscope to the workshop. While he waited, he noticed the drawings Ines had made in the margins of the workshop's order book: leaves, insect wings, the inside of a flower. He asked whether she had ever drawn what she saw through a lens. She had never looked through one.

The order book itself survives. Its margins are filled with objects drawn from whatever was on the workshop bench: a housefly's wing, the seed head of a dandelion, the underside of a leaf. She had no microscope and no training. What she had was the habit of looking at something for a long time before touching a pencil to paper, and a hand trained by four years of painting figures two millimetres high.

Meyer invited her to his laboratory in Lyon. Photography of microscopic samples was still poor at that time; a photograph flattened everything into grey, and important details disappeared. A trained illustrator could do what a camera could not — decide which parts mattered and show them clearly. Ines was employed as a technical assistant in 1923.

The work was slower than anyone expected. A single plate could take three weeks: days at the microscope, then a series of drawings that were shown to the researcher, corrected, and drawn again. Meyer's notebooks record one exchange in which he asked for a structure to be made clearer and she refused, on the grounds that the sample did not show it clearly and the drawing should not claim more than the sample did. He gave way.

Over the next eleven years she produced more than four thousand illustrations for research papers. She never signed them. Scientific illustrations were then regarded as part of the equipment, like a test tube, and the illustrator's name did not appear. Colleagues later recalled that she would sometimes spend a whole day at the microscope before making a single mark on paper, insisting that she could not draw a structure until she understood what it did.

In 1934 she was refused permission to attend a conference in Berlin at which twelve of her illustrations were displayed, because assistants were not invited. She resigned two weeks later.

She was forty-three, unemployed, and without a reference from the laboratory, since technical assistants were not given them.

What followed was unexpected. She opened a small studio and began teaching illustration to science students — first four of them, then thirty. Her argument was simple and, at the time, unusual: a scientist who could draw a specimen would observe it more carefully than one who could only photograph it. Two of her students went on to lead university departments, and both taught drawing to their own students.

Her teaching method was unusual in one respect that her students all mention. She never corrected a drawing. She would ask what the student had seen, listen to the answer, and then send them back to the microscope with a single question — where does that edge actually stop? — and wait. One of them wrote later that it took him two months to understand that she was not being difficult. She had decided that a drawing corrected by someone else teaches nothing, because the error is in the looking and not in the hand.

Ines Bertrand died in 1988. In 1994 a researcher who was matching handwriting in laboratory notebooks identified 3,800 of her unsigned drawings. A collection of them was published in 2001, one hundred years after her birth, under a title she never chose: Seeing First.

questions.stem: What did Ines Bertrand's first paid work require her to do?
choices: Use a very fine brush with great precision.
Repair broken microscopes for customers.
Teach drawing to younger students.
Photograph samples for a laboratory.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Use a very fine brush with great precision.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `work that demanded ~` = 関係代名詞 that が work を修飾。**仕事の中身**を説明
- `a steady hand` =「ぶれない手」= 精密さのコア
- `at sixteen` = `at + 年齢`「16 歳のときに」

## 🔬 文構造分析
`At sixteen she took [a job [painting numbers onto clock faces in her father's workshop]] — [work [that demanded [a steady hand] and [a very fine brush]]].`
  S=she / V=took / O=a job + 現在分詞句 painting ~ が後置修飾
  ダッシュ以下は同格: work + 関係詞節 that demanded A and B

## 📍 本文の根拠
第1段「at sixteen she took a job painting numbers onto clock faces in her father's workshop — **work that demanded a steady hand and a very fine brush**」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Repair broken microscopes for customers.」… 時計を修理していたのは父親 (`Her father repaired clocks`)。主語の取り違え。
- 「Teach drawing to younger students.」… 教える仕事を始めるのは 1934 年の辞職**後**。時期が異なる。
- 「Photograph samples for a laboratory.」… 撮影は当時の研究室の手法として言及されるだけで、彼女の仕事ではない。

questions.stem: Why were drawings preferred to photographs in Meyer's laboratory?
choices: Photography was more expensive than illustration.
Cameras could not be attached to a microscope at all.
An illustrator could choose which details to show clearly.
Researchers were unable to understand photographs.
questions.explanation:
正解は「An illustrator could choose which details to show clearly.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `do what a camera could not` = 関係代名詞 what「カメラにできないこと」
- `decide which parts mattered` = 間接疑問 + `matter` (自動詞「重要である」)
- `flattened everything into grey` = 写真の欠点を示す比喩

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[A trained illustrator] could do [what a camera could not] — [decide [which parts mattered]] and [show them clearly].`
  S=A trained illustrator / V=could do / O=what 節
  ダッシュ以下は what の内容の言い換え (原形不定詞 2 つが and で並列)
    decide + 間接疑問 which parts mattered / show + O=them + M=clearly

## 📍 本文の根拠
第3段「a photograph flattened everything into grey, and important details disappeared. **A trained illustrator could do what a camera could not — decide which parts mattered and show them clearly.**」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Photography was more expensive than illustration.」… 費用についての比較は本文にない。
- 「Cameras could not be attached to a microscope at all.」… `Photography of microscopic samples was still poor at that time` は「質が低かった」であって「使えなかった」ではない。程度の取り違え。
- 「Researchers were unable to understand photographs.」… 研究者が写真を理解できなかったという記述はない。問題は写真の情報が失われることであって、読解力ではない。

questions.stem: Why did her name not appear on her illustrations?
choices: She had asked for her name to be removed from them.
The work of an illustrator was treated as technical support rather than authorship.
Each drawing was made by several people working together.
Her employer published them under his own name by mistake.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The work of an illustrator was treated as technical support rather than authorship.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `were regarded as ~` = 受動態「〜とみなされていた」。**当時の慣行**を示す
- `like a test tube` = 様態の like。「実験器具と同じ扱い」という比喩がコア
- `the illustrator's name did not appear` = 結果としての事実

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[Scientific illustrations] were then regarded [as [part of the equipment], [like a test tube]], and [the illustrator's name did not appear].`
  前半: S=Scientific illustrations / V=were regarded (受動) / C=as part of the equipment / M=like a test tube, then (当時)
  後半: S=the illustrator's name / V=did not appear

## 📍 本文の根拠
第4段「She never signed them. **Scientific illustrations were then regarded as part of the equipment, like a test tube, and the illustrator's name did not appear.**」
個人の事情ではなく当時の分野全体の慣行として説明されている。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「She had asked for her name to be removed from them.」… 本人が削除を求めたという記述はない。慣行として名前が載らなかった。
- 「Each drawing was made by several people working together.」… 共同制作についての記述はない。1994 年に `3,800 of her unsigned drawings` が彼女個人のものと特定されている。
- 「Her employer published them under his own name by mistake.」… 雇用主が自分の名で発表したという記述はなく、`by mistake` を支える根拠もない。

questions.stem: Which of the following shows the correct order of events in her life?
choices: She began teaching → she drew through a microscope → she resigned → her work was published.
She resigned → she drew through a microscope → she began teaching → her work was published.
She drew through a microscope → she resigned → her work was published → she began teaching.
She drew through a microscope → she resigned → she began teaching → her work was published.
questions.explanation:
正解は「She drew through a microscope → she resigned → she began teaching → her work was published.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- 伝記は**西暦**が並べ替えの手がかり。1923 → 1934 → その後 → 2001
- `What followed was unexpected.` = 直前の出来事 (辞職) の**直後**を示すつなぎ
- `She resigned two weeks later` の `later` が基準点からの前後関係を確定させる

## 🔬 文構造分析
`Ines was employed [as a technical assistant] [in 1923].` … 顕微鏡の仕事の開始
`She resigned [two weeks later].` (1934 年の会議拒否の 2 週間後)
`[What followed] was unexpected. She opened a small studio and began teaching ~.`
  S=What followed (関係代名詞 what「続いて起きたこと」) / V=was / C=unexpected
`[A collection of them] was published [in 2001].`

## 📍 本文の根拠
第3段「Ines was employed as a technical assistant in **1923**」→ 第5段「In **1934** she was refused permission ~ She resigned two weeks later.」→ 第6段「**What followed was unexpected.** She opened a small studio and began teaching」→ 最終段「A collection of them was published in **2001**」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「She began teaching → she drew through a microscope → she resigned → her work was published.」… 教え始めたのは辞職後 (`What followed`)。顕微鏡の仕事より前ではない。
- 「She resigned → she drew through a microscope → she began teaching → her work was published.」… 辞職は 1934 年で、顕微鏡の仕事を始めた 1923 年より後。最初の 2 つが逆。
- 「She drew through a microscope → she resigned → her work was published → she began teaching.」… 出版は 2001 年で、教え始めた 1934 年以降より後。最後の 2 つが逆。

  M=more carefully than one who could only photograph it (比較の対象)
  one = a scientist の代名詞

第6段「Her argument was simple and, at the time, unusual: **a scientist who could draw a specimen would observe it more carefully than one who could only photograph it.**」
コロンの後が彼女の主張そのもの。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由

question_data.passage:
You are in a discussion group that is reading about cities and the environment. Read the following article.

MORE TREES IS NOT ALWAYS THE ANSWER

[1] For the past two decades, planting trees has been the most popular answer to almost every urban environmental problem. Cities have announced plans to plant a million trees, and then two million. The appeal is obvious: trees are cheap, they are visible, and nobody objects to them. But researchers who study urban heat have begun to argue that the number of trees a city plants matters far less than where it plants them, and that some planting programmes have produced almost no measurable benefit.

[2] The main way trees cool a city is not by absorbing carbon dioxide, which happens far too slowly to affect summer temperatures, but by providing shade and by releasing water vapour from their leaves. Both effects are strongly local. A tree cools the ground beneath it and the air within a few metres of it; a hundred metres away the difference may be too small to measure. A thousand trees planted in a park on the edge of a city therefore do very little for the crowded central district where the temperature is highest.

[3] Those hot central districts are also, in most cities that have been studied, the districts where the fewest trees already grow, and where residents have the least influence over planning decisions. A survey of thirty-seven cities found that districts with lower average incomes had, on average, 24% less tree cover than wealthier districts in the same city. The gap was not explained by building density: when the researchers compared districts with similar amounts of open ground, it remained. Nor was it explained by preference. Where residents of low-cover districts were asked, they wanted trees at least as much as anyone else, and often more, because they were the ones living with the heat. When a city counts only the total number of trees planted, a programme can look like a complete success while leaving that gap exactly where it was.

[4] There is a further complication. Trees need water, and in dry regions a young tree may require regular watering for its first three to five years. Several cities have found that a large share of the trees they planted did not survive long enough to provide any shade at all. One review of North American programmes estimated that between 15% and 30% of newly planted street trees die within five years, and that survival depends far more on maintenance budgets than on which species is chosen. The pattern is easy to explain once stated. Planting is a single event with a photograph attached to it. Watering is a five-year obligation with nothing to show. Budgets are written by people who need the photograph, and the obligation is left to whoever holds the post in three years' time.

[5] None of this is an argument against planting trees. It is an argument against counting them. A programme that plants two hundred trees along a treeless street in a hot district, waters them for five years and replaces those that die will do more for the people who live there than a programme that plants twenty thousand seedlings and then walks away. The second programme, however, produces a much better headline. It also produces a number that can be compared with last year's number, which is what a city government is usually asked for. A count is easy to audit and impossible to argue with. A measure of shade delivered to the people who need it is neither.

[6] None of the objections above requires new science. They require a city to accept a harder question in place of an easier one, and to keep accepting it after the officials who chose it have moved on. That is an unusual thing for any institution to do, which is why the total keeps being reported.

[7] The question a city should ask is not "how many trees have we planted?" but "how many people are now standing in shade at two o'clock in the afternoon?" That number is harder to collect and much harder to celebrate. It is also the only one that measures what the trees were planted for.
