questions.stem: What is the main point of paragraph [2]?
choices: Trees absorb carbon dioxide faster than researchers expected.
A park on the edge of a city cools the whole city evenly.
The cooling effect of a tree reaches only a short distance from it.
Water vapour released by leaves raises the air temperature.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The cooling effect of a tree reaches only a short distance from it.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `Both effects are strongly local.` = 段落の主題文。`local` =「局所的」がコア
- `not by A but by B` = 冷却の仕組みを A ではなく B と特定する
- `too small to measure` = `too ~ to do`「小さすぎて測れない」

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[The main way [trees cool a city]] is [not by absorbing carbon dioxide ~ but by [providing shade] and [releasing water vapour from their leaves]].`
  S=The main way + 関係詞節 (trees cool a city) / V=is / C=not by A but by B
`A tree cools [the ground beneath it] and [the air within a few metres of it]; [a hundred metres away] [the difference] may be [too small to measure].`
  セミコロンで近距離と遠距離を対比

## 📍 本文の根拠
第2段「**Both effects are strongly local.** A tree cools the ground beneath it and the air within a few metres of it; a hundred metres away the difference may be too small to measure.」
この主題文と具体化が段落全体を支配している。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Trees absorb carbon dioxide faster than researchers expected.」… `absorbing carbon dioxide, which happens far too slowly to affect summer temperatures` と、むしろ遅いと否定されている。
- 「A park on the edge of a city cools the whole city evenly.」… 同段落末で `A thousand trees planted in a park on the edge of a city therefore do very little for the crowded central district` と、都市全体には効かないと明言。
- 「Water vapour released by leaves raises the air temperature.」… 蒸散 (releasing water vapour) は**冷却**の仕組みとして挙げられている。効果の向きが逆。

questions.stem: According to paragraph [3], what can a tree-planting programme hide?
choices: The unequal distribution of trees between richer and poorer districts.
The high cost of buying young trees.
The difficulty of finding space in which to plant.
The slow growth rate of native species.
questions.explanation:
正解は「The unequal distribution of trees between richer and poorer districts.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `while leaving that gap exactly where it was` = 付帯状況の while + 分詞。「格差をそのままにしたまま」
- `can look like a complete success` = 見かけ上の成功。**実態との乖離**がこの段落の主張
- `24% less tree cover` = 差を示す比較表現

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[When a city counts only the total number of trees planted], [a programme] can look [like a complete success] [while leaving [that gap] [exactly where it was]].`
  従属節: S=a city / V=counts / O=only the total number of trees planted
  主節: S=a programme / V=can look / C=like a complete success
  while 分詞句: leaving + O=that gap + C=exactly where it was (格差は元のまま)

## 📍 本文の根拠
第3段「A survey of thirty-seven cities found that districts with lower average incomes had, on average, 24% less tree cover than wealthier districts in the same city. ~ **When a city counts only the total number of trees planted, a programme can look like a complete success while leaving that gap exactly where it was.**」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「The high cost of buying young trees.」… 苗木の価格については `trees are cheap` と第1段にあり、高コストは論点ではない。
- 「The difficulty of finding space in which to plant.」… 植える場所の確保が難しいという記述はない。論点は「どこに植えるか」の選択であって用地不足ではない。
- 「The slow growth rate of native species.」… 成長速度についての記述はない。第4段の論点は生存率であって成長率ではない。

questions.stem: According to paragraph [4], what most affects whether a newly planted street tree survives?
choices: Which species of tree is chosen.
How old the tree is when it is planted.
How many trees are planted at the same time.
How much money is available to look after it.
questions.explanation:
正解は「How much money is available to look after it.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `depends far more on A than on B` = 比較級の強調 `far more`。**A の方が決定的**
- `maintenance budgets` = 維持管理予算。ここが生存率の決定要因
- `than on which species is chosen` = 比較対象として樹種を明示的に退ける

## 🔬 文構造分析
`One review ~ estimated [that [between 15% and 30% of newly planted street trees] die [within five years]], and [that [survival] depends [far more on maintenance budgets] than [on which species is chosen]].`
  S=One review / V=estimated / O=that 節 × 2 (and で並列)
  第2の that 節: S=survival / V=depends / M=far more on A than on B
    A=maintenance budgets / B=which species is chosen (間接疑問)

## 📍 本文の根拠
第4段「**survival depends far more on maintenance budgets than on which species is chosen**」
`far more ~ than` が予算 > 樹種 という優劣を明示している。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Which species of tree is chosen.」… `than on which species is chosen` で、比較対象として**退けられている**側。far more A than B の B にあたる。
- 「How old the tree is when it is planted.」… 植えるときの樹齢についての記述はない。
- 「How many trees are planted at the same time.」… 同時に植える本数は第5段の論点 (総数主義への批判) だが、個々の木の生存率の決定要因としては挙げられていない。

questions.stem: What does the author mean by "It is an argument against counting them" in paragraph [5]?
choices: Cities should stop keeping any records of the trees they plant.
Programmes should be judged by their effects rather than by their totals.
Cities should plant fewer trees than they do at present.
Cities should not report the results of their programmes to the public.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Programmes should be judged by their effects rather than by their totals.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `None of this is an argument against planting trees.` = 直前で**植樹自体は否定していない**と断る
- `It is an argument against counting them.` = 対比。否定されるのは**数えること**
- `counting` = 総本数を成果指標にすること、の言い換え

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[None of this] is [an argument against planting trees]. [It] is [an argument against counting them].`
  第1文: S=None of this / V=is / C=an argument against planting trees (植樹への反対を否定)
  第2文: S=It / V=is / C=an argument against counting them
  → against の目的語が planting → counting に置き換わる対比構造

## 📍 本文の根拠
第5段「**None of this is an argument against planting trees. It is an argument against counting them.**」に続いて、200 本を 5 年間手入れする計画の方が 20,000 本植えて放置する計画より住民の役に立つ、と具体化される。
最終段の「how many people are now standing in shade」も同じ主張の言い換え。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Cities should stop keeping any records of the trees they plant.」… 記録すること自体の否定ではない。最終段は**別の指標で測れ**と提案しており、計測の放棄ではない。
- 「Cities should plant fewer trees than they do at present.」… 本数を減らせとは述べていない。`None of this is an argument against planting trees` と明確に断っている。
- 「Cities should not report the results of their programmes to the public.」… 公表をやめよとは述べていない。むしろ `much harder to celebrate` な数値を採れと求めている。

questions.stem: Which title best expresses the author's argument?
choices: Why cities should stop planting trees in hot districts
The evidence that trees do not cool cities at all
Where a city plants matters more than how many trees it plants
How planting a million trees solved one city's heat problem
questions.explanation:
正解は「Where a city plants matters more than how many trees it plants」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- タイトル問題は**第1段の主張文**と**最終段の結論**の両方に整合するものを選ぶ
- `matters far less than where it plants them` = 「どこに植えるか」>「何本植えるか」
- 本文が否定していない事柄まで否定する選択肢は不適

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[researchers ~] have begun to argue [that [the number of trees a city plants] matters [far less than [where it plants them]]], and [that [some planting programmes] have produced [almost no measurable benefit]].`
  S=researchers / V=have begun to argue / O=that 節 × 2
  第1の that 節: S=the number of trees a city plants / V=matters / M=far less than where ~

## 📍 本文の根拠
第1段「**the number of trees a city plants matters far less than where it plants them**」
最終段「The question a city should ask is not "how many trees have we planted?" but "**how many people are now standing in shade at two o'clock in the afternoon?**"」
冒頭の主張と結末の問いが一致している。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Why cities should stop planting trees in hot districts」… 暑い地区こそ植えるべきだというのが本文の主張。正反対。
- 「The evidence that trees do not cool cities at all」… `None of this is an argument against planting trees` および第2段の冷却機構の説明と矛盾する。冷却効果そのものは否定されていない。
- 「How planting a million trees solved one city's heat problem」… 100 万本規模の計画は第1段・第5段で**批判の対象**として挙げられている。解決事例ではない。

question_data.passage:
You are making a poster for a school project on food waste. Read the following article and organise the information.

WHERE FOOD IS LOST

[1] Roughly a third of the food produced for people to eat is never eaten. That figure is quoted so often that it has stopped meaning very much. It hides the more useful question: at which point does the food disappear, and does the answer differ from country to country?

[2] It does, and sharply. In lower-income countries most losses happen early, between the field and the market. Crops are damaged by insects during storage, or spoil in transport because there is no refrigeration, or simply cannot reach a buyer before they rot. Very little is thrown away by households, because food is expensive relative to income and people are careful with it.

[3] The difference is not a matter of care. A farmer in either place has the same reason to get a crop to market. What differs is the chain between the two: whether there is a cold store within reach, whether the road holds up in the rain, whether a buyer can be found in the two days the crop will keep. Where those things are missing, food is lost before anyone has had the chance to decide anything about it.

[4] In higher-income countries the pattern is reversed. Storage and transport are efficient, and losses before the shop are comparatively small. The waste happens at the end of the chain: in supermarkets, in restaurants and, above all, in homes. In several European studies, households were responsible for between 45% and 55% of all the food wasted in the country — more than farms, factories, shops and restaurants combined.

[5] Household waste is also the hardest kind to reduce, because it is not one behaviour but many. A shopper buys three peppers because they are sold in a pack of three, uses one, and finds the others soft a week later. A family cooks for four when three are eating. A label reading "best before" is understood as if it read "use by", and a perfectly good yoghurt goes into the bin. A restaurant portion arrives larger than anyone ordered because a small plate looks like poor value. A household buys for the week it plans to have rather than the week it will have, and Thursday's plan collapses on Tuesday. Each of these has a different solution, and none of those solutions is a poster telling people not to waste food.

[6] This is why the measures that work best tend to be structural rather than educational. When one supermarket chain removed date labels from fresh fruit and vegetables — items for which the label adds no safety information — waste of those items in customers' homes fell measurably. When another chain allowed customers to buy single items instead of fixed packs, sales of the affected products fell slightly while waste fell a great deal more. A third removed multi-buy offers on fresh produce and replaced them with a lower single price. Customers bought less and threw away much less, and the chain reported that revenue on those items was almost unchanged, because the lower price brought in buyers who had previously bought nothing.

[7] Educational campaigns are not useless, but their effects fade. Studies of household campaigns generally show a reduction while the campaign is running and a return to earlier levels within a year of its end. One reason may be that a campaign asks people to remember something new every time they shop, while a change to the packet asks nothing of them at all. Changes to the way food is sold, by contrast, keep working whether or not anyone is paying attention.

[8] There is a further reason to start with measurement rather than with a campaign. A country that assumes its losses are where the headline says they are will spend its money in the wrong place, and will then conclude that food waste is hard to reduce. It is not especially hard to reduce. It is hard to reduce without first knowing which of several quite different problems you actually have.

[9] For a country deciding where to act, then, the first step is not a slogan. It is to find out where in its own food chain the food is actually being lost — and to accept that the answer for one country is not the answer for another.

questions.stem: Why does the author say that the figure "a third of all food" has "stopped meaning very much"?
choices: It is based on research that is now out of date.
It does not show at which stage of the food chain the loss happens.
It is too small a share to be a serious problem.
It applies only to lower-income countries.
questions.explanation:
正解は「It does not show at which stage of the food chain the loss happens.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `It hides the more useful question` = `hide`「覆い隠す」。**数字が問いを隠す**が主張
- `at which point does the food disappear` = 前置詞 + 関係詞の間接疑問
- `has stopped meaning very much` = 現在完了「意味を持たなくなってしまった」

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[That figure] is quoted [so often] [that it has stopped meaning very much]. [It] hides [the more useful question]: [at which point does the food disappear], and [does the answer differ from country to country]?`
  第1文: so ~ that 構文 (あまりに頻繁に引用され、その結果〜)
  第2文: S=It (= that figure) / V=hides / O=the more useful question
  コロン以下がその question の中身 (2 つの疑問文)

## 📍 本文の根拠
第1段「That figure is quoted so often that it has stopped meaning very much. **It hides the more useful question: at which point does the food disappear, and does the answer differ from country to country?**」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「It is based on research that is now out of date.」… 数字が古いとは述べていない。問題にしているのは**内訳が見えないこと**。
- 「It is too small a share to be a serious problem.」… `Roughly a third` は小さい割合ではなく、深刻さを示す数字として引用されている。
- 「It applies only to lower-income countries.」… 第2段以降で低所得国と高所得国の**両方**を扱っており、適用範囲の限定は誤り。

questions.stem: According to paragraph [2], why do households in lower-income countries waste little food?
choices: They have better refrigeration than richer countries.
They buy most of their food already cooked.
Their governments fine households that waste food.
Food takes up a large share of their income, so they use it carefully.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Food takes up a large share of their income, so they use it carefully.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `expensive relative to income` = `relative to`「〜に比べて」。**所得比での高さ**がコア
- `be careful with ~` =「〜を大事に扱う」
- `because` が理由を直接示す

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[Very little] is thrown away [by households], [because [food is expensive relative to income] and [people are careful with it]].`
  主節: S=Very little / V=is thrown away (受動) / M=by households
  because 節: 2 文が and で並列
    S=food / V=is / C=expensive relative to income ・ S=people / V=are careful with it

## 📍 本文の根拠
第2段「Very little is thrown away by households, **because food is expensive relative to income and people are careful with it.**」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「They have better refrigeration than richer countries.」… 同じ段落に `spoil in transport because there is no refrigeration` とあり、冷蔵設備は**ない**。正反対。
- 「They buy most of their food already cooked.」… 調理済み食品の購入についての記述はない。
- 「Their governments fine households that waste food.」… 罰金などの政策についての記述はない。

questions.stem: What do the European studies mentioned in paragraph [3] show?
choices: Restaurants waste more food than homes do.
Losses during transport are the largest single category.
Homes account for more waste than all the other stages put together.
Supermarkets waste about half of the food they receive.
questions.explanation:
正解は「Homes account for more waste than all the other stages put together.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `more than A, B, C and D combined` = 「A〜D を合わせたより多い」。**combined** が急所
- `be responsible for ~` =「〜の原因である・〜を占める」
- `between 45% and 55%` = 幅を持った割合

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[In several European studies], [households] were responsible for [between 45% and 55% of all the food wasted in the country] — [more than [farms, factories, shops and restaurants] combined].`
  S=households / V=were responsible for / O=between 45% and 55% ~
  ダッシュ以下が比較の補足: more than A, B, C and D combined

## 📍 本文の根拠
第4段「**households were responsible for between 45% and 55% of all the food wasted in the country — more than farms, factories, shops and restaurants combined.**」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Restaurants waste more food than homes do.」… レストランは家庭より少ない側として列挙されている。大小が逆。
- 「Losses during transport are the largest single category.」… 第4段冒頭に `losses before the shop are comparatively small` とあり、高所得国では輸送段階の損失は小さい。
- 「Supermarkets waste about half of the food they receive.」… 45〜55% は**家庭**の割合。スーパーマーケットの数値ではない。数値の係り先の取り違え。

questions.stem: Why does the author call household waste "the hardest kind to reduce"?
choices: It comes from many different habits, each needing a different solution.
Households refuse to take part in surveys about it.
The amount wasted in homes cannot be measured at all.
It occurs only in the wealthiest countries.
questions.explanation:
正解は「It comes from many different habits, each needing a different solution.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `not one behaviour but many` = not A but B。**単一の行動ではなく多数**
- `Each of these has a different solution` = だから対策も一つにならない
- `read as if it read "use by"` = 仮定法の as if。表示の誤読を示す

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[Household waste] is also [the hardest kind to reduce], [because [it] is [not one behaviour but many]].`
  主節: S=Household waste / V=is / C=the hardest kind to reduce (不定詞が kind を修飾)
  because 節: S=it / V=is / C=not one behaviour but many (= many behaviours)
  → 続く 3 つの具体例 (3 個パック・作りすぎ・表示の誤読) が many の中身

## 📍 本文の根拠
第5段「Household waste is also the hardest kind to reduce, **because it is not one behaviour but many.**」
3 つの例のあとに「**Each of these has a different solution**」と締められる。

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「Households refuse to take part in surveys about it.」… 調査への非協力についての記述はない。
- 「The amount wasted in homes cannot be measured at all.」… 第4段で家庭の割合が数値化されており、測定できている。
- 「It occurs only in the wealthiest countries.」… 第2段で低所得国の家庭についても論じており、富裕国限定ではない。

Their effect tends to disappear after the campaign ends.

questions.explanation:
正解は「Their effect tends to disappear after the campaign ends.」。

## 🎯 コアイメージ
- `their effects fade` = `fade`「薄れる」。**効果の減衰**がこの段落の主張
- `a return to earlier levels within a year of its end` = 終了後 1 年以内に元の水準へ戻る
- `not useless, but ~` = 全否定ではない譲歩。断定の強さに注意

## 🔬 文構造分析
`[Educational campaigns] are [not useless], but [their effects fade]. Studies ~ show [a reduction [while the campaign is running]] and [a return to earlier levels [within a year of its end]].`
  第1文: S=Educational campaigns / V=are / C=not useless ・ S=their effects / V=fade
  第2文: S=Studies / V=show / O=a reduction と a return (等位接続)

## 📍 本文の根拠
第7段「Educational campaigns are not useless, but **their effects fade.** Studies of household campaigns generally show a reduction while the campaign is running and **a return to earlier levels within a year of its end.**」

## ❌ 誤答 NG 理由
- 「They are more effective than changing the way food is sold.」… 第6段は `the measures that work best tend to be structural rather than educational` とし、販売方法の変更の方が有効だと述べている。優劣が逆。
- 「They have no effect on household behaviour at all.」… `Educational campaigns are not useless` と明示的に否定されている。「全く効果がない」は本文より強すぎる。
- 「They work best in lower-income countries.」… 低所得国との関連づけは本文にない。
